claims.quote: the books of every nation are examined. If France is found in our debt, probably we are in the debt of some nation which owes France, and so on with all the nations.
claims.description: An international council audits and clears the trade balances of nations, which settle in national staples rather than money.

claims.quote: An American in Berlin takes his credit card to the local office of the international council, and receives in exchange for the whole or part of it a German credit card, the amount being charged against the United States in favor of Germany on the international account.
claims.description: A moneyless economy uses national credit cards exchanged between countries via an international council.

claims.quote: if a man at twenty-one emigrates from England to America, England loses all the expense of his maintenance and education, and America gets a workman for nothing. America accordingly makes England an allowance.
claims.description: Emigration is regulated by indemnity payments between nations for the cost of raising each worker.

claims.quote: Not only is our cooking done at the public kitchens, as I told you last night, but the service and quality of the meals are much more satisfactory if taken at the dining-house.
claims.description: Cooking is done in public kitchens and most people dine in ward dining-houses.

claims.quote: a continuous waterproof covering had been let down so as to inclose the sidewalk and turn it into a well lighted and perfectly dry corridor
claims.description: City sidewalks are roofed by retractable waterproof coverings in rain.

claims.quote: The waiters are young men in the unclassified grade of the industrial army who are assignable to all sorts of miscellaneous occupations not requiring special skill.
claims.description: All citizens serve in a national industrial army, with young recruits given assorted jobs.

claims.quote: The equal wealth and equal opportunities of culture which all persons now enjoy have simply made us all members of one class, which corresponds to the most fortunate class with you.
claims.description: Equal wealth and education abolish class distinctions and the stigma of menial service.

claims.quote: It is bound to print all that is offered it, but prints it only on condition that the author defray the first cost out of his credit.
claims.description: A national printing department publishes any book an author pays for from personal credit, with no censorship.

claims.quote: They vote upon the acceptance of statues and paintings for the public buildings, and their favorable verdict carries with it the artist's remission from other tasks to devote himself to his vocation.
claims.description: The public votes on art for public buildings and successful artists are released from other labor.

claims.quote: The highest of all honors in the nation, higher than the presidency, which calls merely for good sense and devotion to duty, is the red ribbon awarded by the vote of the people to the great authors, artists, engineers, physicians, and inventors of the generation.
claims.description: National honor, a red ribbon voted by the people, outranks political office.

claims.quote: The people who take the paper pay the expense of its publication, choose its editor, and remove him when unsatisfactory.
claims.description: Newspapers are published by the nation but funded by subscribers who elect and dismiss the editor.

claims.quote: There ensued an era of mechanical invention, scientific discovery, art, musical and literary productiveness to which no previous age of the world offers anything comparable.
claims.description: The new social order unleashes an unprecedented flowering of invention, science and the arts.

claims.quote: Till the war-drum throbbed no longer, and the battle-flags were furled.
claims.description: A poetic vision of the end of war.

claims.quote: In the Parliament of man, the federation of the world.
claims.description: A poetic vision of a world federation and parliament of humanity.
